title: 35. SURGICAL CAUSES OF ACUTE ABDOMINAL PAIN IN PREGNANCY:

blocks.content:
35. SURGICAL CAUSES OF ACUTE ABDOMINAL PAIN IN PREGNANCY:

•1 in 500 – 635 pregnancies.
•Early senior surgeon opinion should be sought.

D/D of abdominal pain in Pregnancy:

1.Obstetric causes.
2.Surgical.
3.Non-surgical.

 

1.Obstetric causes:

Early: late:

i.Miscarriage. i. Abruption
ii.Ectopic ii. Labour.
iii.Urinary retention. iii. Rupture.
iv.Fibroids degeneration. iv. AFLP/PE
v.Round ligaments pain. v. Chorioamnionitis.

vi. Symphysis pubis dysfunction.

vii. Fibroid degeneration.

viii. Braxton hicks.

2.Surgical:
i.Appendicitis.
ii.cholecystitis Biliary colic.
iii.pancreatitis.
iv.Peptic ulcer.
v.Bowel obs.
vi.Ureteric obs.
vii.Aneurysm rupture.
3.Non – Surgical:
i.Pyelonephritis.
ii.IBD
iii.Ovarian cyst accident.
iv.Constipation.
v.Pneumonia.
vi.Psychogenic.
vii.Trauma – abuse.
viii.MI.
ix.DKA. Rare.
x.Prophylaxis

History:

•Evaluation of presenting symptoms.
•Past obstetric, medical, surgical history.
•Don’t forget to inquire about trauma, Abuse

Characteristics of Pain:

Site:

•Focal, sharp, finger, pointing => peritoneal pain.
•Poorly localized/ segmented => visceral.
→Foregut – upper abdominal pain.
→Mid gut – around umbilicus.
→Hind gut – lower abdominal pain
→Shoulder tip – haemoperitoneum/ visceral leakage.

Quality of Pain:

•Colicky – Obstruction of hollow viscus ureter, biliary duct.
•Burning –
1.Peptic ulcer.
2.Esophageal
3.Pancreatitis.
•Constant – peritoneal inflammation.

Duration and Timing:

Exacerbating & Reliving Factors

-Visceral pain – restlessness
-Perinatal injury/ irritation – exaggerate with pain

Associated symptoms:

Examination: General + abdominal

Physiological changes

•Blood volume = 40%
•Co = 10 – 30%
•HR – from 70 = 80-90bpm
•O2 consumption = 20%
•Temperature
•Tidal volume 500 – 700ml

Anatomical changes:

Gravid uterus

-Shift appendix in upper Quadrant
-Hamper free fluid
-Difficulty in assessing site of tenderness

 

Let women on her site

 

Then check tenderness, if remain same then non uterine.

-Difficulty assessing mass

 

Turn on side then palpate

Hydroureters – 2cm

Hydronephrosis

-Right - >15mm
-Left - >5m

(pelvicalyceal diameter)

Clinical Red Flags:

1.Readmission
2.Repeated doses of opiates given for analgesia without a cause of pain being established
3.New onset anxiety & confusion being attributed to psychiatric rather than underlying organic cause

Investigation:

Bed side

-Pulse, B.P, RR, Temp, O2 sat
-Urine dip
🡩> 1+ protein urea => Quantification
-ECG – epigastric/ upper abdominal pain + risk factor for MI

Biochemical:

-FBC – TLC normal up to (5.9 – 15.6 x 109)
-CRP – (N – 20mg/dl)

-Creatinine – up to 0.8
-ABGS – physiological hyperventilation PO2, PCO2, HCO3
-Lactate for tissue perfusion.

Imaging:

•USG – 1st line for appendicitis:
-90% inconclusive.
-Sensitivity 60%.
-Specificity – 100%.
•X – ray erect abdomen - CXR with shield is safe.

Dose up to 10m GY is negligible in 1st , risk of childhood cancer 0.002%.

•MRI safe
•CT – avoid – childhood CA 0.1 – 0.3%.

Management MDT input:

OBS consideration:

•Miscarriage risk 0.7%.
•PTB 3.2%.
•Laparoscopy more risk of miscarriage but equal risk of PTB.
→After 20 weeks – left lateral tilt during surgery.
→Steroid 24 – 34 + 6 weeks.
→Fetal monitoring:
-Early – Auscultation.
-Late – CTG.
→VTE prophylaxis.
→Anti D – whenever uterine manipulation done.

Surgical consideration:

•MDT.
•Incisions according to pregnancy duration & surgical condition
•Appendix shifting upward as pregnancy advances.
